convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load WPR_Histogram custom indicator (not built-in), and depends on external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for all trade execution functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose). Custom indicator logic is opaque without its source.

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - seconds per bar of the indicator timeframe
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime and DnSignalTime calculation for position open timing

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars required for indicator to be ready

other_exits: Buy position closed when WPR_Histogram buffer 1 equals 2 (sell zone); Sell position closed when WPR_Histogram buffer 1 equals 0 (buy zone)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum controls sizing: LOT=fixed lot size of MM=0.1; FREEMARGIN/BALANCE/LOSSFREEMARGIN/LOSSBALANCE=fraction of equity/balance/free margin as percentage determined by MM value

custom_logic_notes: The WPR_Histogram custom indicator has 3 buffers (indices 0,1,2). Buffer 2 (color buffer) is read with CopyBuffer to determine zone: value 0 = buy zone (WPR above HighLevel=-30), value 2 = sell zone (WPR below LowLevel=-70). Buffer 0 is the histogram value. Entry signal: if color buffer[1]==0 AND histogram[0]>0 → buy; if color buffer[1]==2 AND histogram[0]<2 → sell. The SignalBar input (default=1) means signals are read from the previous closed bar, not the current bar. When SignalBar=0, signals are evaluated on every tick (intrabar). UpSignalTime/DnSignalTime are set to last bar time + timeframe seconds, used as expiry/time-reference for the trade execution functions. The EA uses GlobalVariableDel_ on deinit for cleanup. Close signals are generated independently from open signals based on the opposite zone detection.
python_conversion_notes: Requires reverse-engineering the WPR_Histogram custom indicator logic: it appears to be a colored WPR histogram where WPR values above -30 are colored as buy zone (buffer color=0) and below -70 as sell zone (buffer color=2), with a neutral zone between. The WPR itself is a built-in indicator (iWPR), so the histogram can likely be replicated by computing WPR and classifying into zones. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose - these must be reimplemented with standard MT5 Python API order placement logic. Position sizing has 5 modes via MarginMode enum. The SignalBar=1 default means evaluating the signal on the last closed bar - equivalent to using shifted data in Python. SL/TP are in points (1000/2000) which may need digit-adjustment for 5-digit brokers - verify whether TradeAlgorithms.mqh handles this internally or if raw point values are passed to OrderSend.
